name: QWEN-LOW-DEFAULT-1
note: Machine-readable form of PRE-REG QWEN-LOW-DEFAULT-1; the prose governs on any conflict. Artin's release-engineering GO (2026-10-23) after VERDICT QWEN-LOW-RELEASE-0 was HELD on its bar 9: the operational cache-correctness contract is registered as the decision, and the chat defaults (Session and CLI with no controls given: enable_thinking True, reasoning_effort low, 768 tokens, incremental reuse under the exact-prefix check with replay fallback, greedy, generation 5) are promoted if the contract passes a FRESH integration smoke. The contract: reuse the cache only when the rendered transcript has the previously fed ids as an exact prefix; otherwise replay with the reason recorded; never reuse an incompatible cache; generated tokens equal full replay where qualified; every measured KV offset equals the accounting; fallback frequency and latency are operational metrics, not failures. The v3 quality receipts and the four-conversation receipt of QWEN-LOW-RELEASE-0 are prior evidence already read, cited, not re-run and not a new blind confirmation; the historical HOLD stands as booked. The defaults are changed in code at this registration so the smoke tests the actual defaults; any bar other than FIRE reverts them in the HOLD commit. AMENDED by AMENDMENT QWEN-LOW-DEFAULT-1-SMOKE (drafted while the first smoke was live, before its receipt was read, from the Opus review): the first smoke's receipt (logs/qwen_release/default1_smoke.json) was written by a test whose context-cap input was too short to trip the cap and by a driver without a guard on a non-reproducing fixture, with bar 6 able to pass on skipped live tests and bars 1, 2 and 5 able to pass with no reuse exercised; the smoke is repaired and re-run into logs/qwen_release/default1_smoke_2.json with the serve suite added, validity floors (no skipped live tests; at least 4 of 6 later smoke turns reused) and an independent re-rendering behind bar 1; the fixture bar now requires the registered break offset 47 and the receipt's prompt sha; the revert values on HOLD are Session enable_thinking None and reasoning_effort None (the template's default), DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS 512, CLI --max-tokens 512 and thinking None, with tests/test_qdefaults.py and tests/test_qrelease.py rewritten in the same commit; an aborted smoke or a missing receipt is a HOLD. Bars, values and the decision rule unchanged.

refuted_if: The promotion is HELD and the defaults reverted if any bar reads other than FIRE: an unsafe or incompatible reuse, a token difference against replay, an offset mismatch, a fixture that does not reproduce or does not replay, or a failing release test; the failing bar and its value are the HOLD's evidence.
registered_prior: The contract already held on every measured turn of QWEN-CHAT-DEFAULT-0 (32 of 32), QWEN-DEEPCHAT-0 (24 of 24) and QWEN-LOW-RELEASE-0 (32 of 32 with one benign fallback), so bars 1, 2, 3 and 5 are expected FIRE at 0. The fixture is expected to reproduce exactly (greedy on the same ids; the merge is a property of the tokenizer, not the model) with the fallback's first token near a 1,851-token replay prefill (about 50 s) against 2 to 3 s for an incremental turn: the latency cost of a fallback is the operational metric this registration reports. The release tests are expected to pass; the likeliest failure is a live timing or environment flake, which would read as a HOLD to be understood, not a defect of the contract.
